findings.text: the agent read does not revalidate its rows by stat identity on every call: index_rows returns the cached IndexBuild for a (project, docs_dir, with_git) key whenever one is present (metadata_index.py:122) and reaches build_index — the only place a file's stat identity is compared (metadata_index.py:158) — on a miss alone, while the MCP/CLI process runs no change watch and nothing in reckon/mcp.py or reckon/mcp_views.py calls metadata_index.invalidate_tree (only reckon/serve.py:1499 does, from the watch at serve.py:295); reproduced at 2cc4f81a6 with a project summary built cold reading "Original title", the file rewritten, a second summary in the same process still reading "Original title", and a rebuild after metadata_index.clear() reading "CHANGED title", so a file changed under a live MCP process is answered from a superseded snapshot until that process restarts.

the measure clears metadata_index.clear() (and file_memo) immediately before each counted read, so it exercises the cold path only and cannot show a warm read; no case calls a view twice with a changed file in one process, which is why the staleness above is unguarded and would fail no assertion.

item_verdicts.diff: read ac9beac9f in full — it adds index_discovery and its helpers at reckon/mcp_views.py:1132-1250 and _index_project_summary, _index_sprint_state and _aggregate_version at reckon/mcp.py:1705-1810, switches the project-summary and sprint-summary branches onto them, drops a count the index cannot derive rather than reporting it as zero, and adds 224 lines of test; the fragment commit 2cc4f81a6 adds only the evidence page and no source.
item_verdicts.done_when: the measure builds a 200-document temporary project over a temporary configuration home, asserts a project-level summary and a sprint summary read (walks, meta parses, full parses) = (0, 0, 0) after the in-process memos are cleared, and names the negative control that routes the views through discover_plans again; I reran the head arm myself (112 passed, EXIT=0 at 2cc4f81a6) and reproduced the negative control on a scratch copy of the tree ((2, 200, 0) == (0, 0, 0), 2 failed 1 passed, EXIT=1), so the guard fires.
item_verdicts.goal: §8 asks agent readers to take list-level facts from reckon.metadata_index — the same module and the same persisted file the served process uses — and derive heavier state only for the resource they were asked about; reckon/mcp_views.py:1132 index_discovery reads metadata_index.index_rows for the inventory and the project's own state document for sprints, milestones, blockers and timeline, and reckon/mcp.py routes the project-level summary (mcp.py:1315) and the sprint summary (mcp.py:1420) through it while view=detail, view=raw and a body search keep the derived path.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it declares status complete with commits ac9beac9f and 2cc4f81a6, records the base arm as 109 passed and the head arm as 112 passed in JSON carrying completed true, and names the negative-control log; head-gate.log and base-gate.log each name their revision on the first line and end with a bare EXIT=0, and the manifest's counts reconcile with both.
item_verdicts.write_paths: `git diff --numstat 4bdf93dde 2cc4f81a6` lists exactly four files — reckon/mcp.py, reckon/mcp_views.py, tests/test_agent_readers_use_the_index.py and docs/evidence/fragments/the-page-paints-from-an-index/agent-readers-use-the-index.html — every one inside the five declared paths; the declared figures directory was touched by nothing.

justifications.durability: the cold path is properly held — a positive control proves the counters fire, the negative control proves they catch a return to discover_plans, and the test fixtures are deterministic (temporary trees, fixed slugs, no date-derived literal) — but the behaviour it lands has an untested warm cycle: nothing in the suite calls a view twice with a changed file in one process, so the staleness the finding names would fail no assertion.
justifications.evidence: the measure is genuine and guarded — a positive control (the cold build parses all 200 documents), a declared negative control I reproduced myself ((2, 200, 0), 2 failed, EXIT=1), and gate logs at base (109 passed) and head (112 passed) that reconcile with the manifest; the deduction is that every counted read is preceded by metadata_index.clear() and file_memo.clear(), so the zero can only demonstrate the cold path and cannot distinguish a reader that revalidates each call from one that serves a cached build — the exact property the review question asks about.
justifications.fit: the new symbols are named by mechanism (index_discovery, _index_project_summary, _index_sprint_state, _aggregate_version, _indexed_item) with docstrings that state why the index is the source, the code carries no plan, phase, ticket or version label, and the one "Claude" hit in reckon/mcp.py:14 is the pre-existing MCP-client usage note, not self-attribution.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the thin interface is real and routed — index_discovery reads metadata_index.index_rows for the list rows and the project state document for the rest, the project summary and sprint summary take that payload, and detail/raw/search keep the derived path as §8's "derive heavier state only for the resource they were asked about" requires; the deduction is that §8 names "the same persisted file the served process uses", and on a warm process the read answers from neither a re-read of that file nor a stat check but from the in-process build (see the finding), so the stated identity with the served process holds on the cold call only.
justifications.scope_discipline: `git diff --numstat 4bdf93dde 2cc4f81a6` lists four changed files, all within the five declared write paths, the reviewer's own tree is untouched, and no plan or index state was edited.
